statement: For all subsets A and B of any topological space, the closure of the intersection equals the intersection of the closures: cl(A intersect B) = cl(A) intersect cl(B).
definitions: cl(S) denotes the closure of S in the ambient topological space X (the smallest closed set containing S); A and B are arbitrary subsets of X.
ground_truth_witness: Take X = {1, 2} with the indiscrete topology (open sets [] and [1,2]) and let A = {1}, B = {2}. Then A intersect B is empty, so cl(A intersect B) is empty, while cl(A) = cl(B) = X, so cl(A) intersect cl(B) = X. Only the inclusion cl(A intersect B) inside cl(A) intersect cl(B) holds in general.

verification_note: Topology axioms checked; the one-sided inclusion is verified for all 16 pairs of subsets, and the strict failure of equality is verified at the witness pair.
book_citation: Lynn Arthur Steen and J. Arthur Seebach Jr., Counterexamples in Topology, 2nd ed., Springer-Verlag, 1978 (Dover reprint, 1995), Example 4 (Indiscrete topology)

skeptic.objection: Precise and false; witness verified (in the 2-point indiscrete space cl({1} cap {2}) = empty while cl({1}) cap cl({2}) = X). Near-trivial: A = (0,1), B = (1,2) in R refutes it in one line, so difficulty 1; still a construction rather than recall of a famous object. No roster/surplus overlap.
